# dsh-net-proxy
**Paste this into your AI agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, DeepSeek Harness — anything that can ru
n commands) and it will install and configure this plugin for you:**
[代码示例省略，未执行]
*A self-contained outbound proxy for the DeepSeek Harness desktop app.*
中文说明

> **You need a subscription.** This plugin is a *client*. It does not sell, provide or
> bypass anyt

hing by itself — bring a Clash-format subscription link from whatever
> provider you already use. Wi
thout one it has no nodes to connect through.
## What it does
Paste a Clash subscription link once. The plugin then:

1. **Starts its own proxy core** — a bundled mihomo binary, so nothing else has to be installed
2. *

*Measures every node itself** against `https://github.com`, concurrently
3. **Uses the fastest one**

, and switches automatically when a node dies
4. **Routes the agent's traffic through it** — `web_fe
tch`, model calls, and child processes like `git` and `npm`
No Clash client running in the background. No system proxy. No hosts file. No admin rights.
## Why it exists

Asking an agent to work with GitHub from a censored network goes like this: the request
times out, t

he agent concludes the network is broken, and you end up explaining your proxy
setup by hand, every

concludes the network is broken, and you end up explaining your proxy
setup by hand, every session.
The usual fixes do not fit an agent:

- **A system proxy** is invisible to it — `fetch` inside a Node process does not use one.
- **A GUI

proxy client** may not be running, and the agent cannot start a GUI app from its sandbox.
- **The cl

ient's own `url-test` group** re-tests on a fixed interval (often daily) against
`gstatic.com`, whic

h is not the site you actually care about, and it does not re-test when
a request fails.

So this plugin measures the thing that matters, when it matters, and switches when a request
fails.
## Install
### The one-prompt way

Copy the block at the top of this file into an agent that can run shell commands. It has
everything

it needs: the repo URL, where the profile lives, which tools to run, and how to
verify the result.
### By hand
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The core and geodata are **committed to this repository**, so step 5 is the last one —
there is noth

ing to download. If you want to refresh them later (or you stripped them out
to keep the clone small
), see THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md.
## Use
Open **Settings → Network proxy**.

- **First time:** paste your subscription link, press **Update subscription**
- **Every other time:*

* press **Enable proxy**. That is the whole flow — it starts the core,
ranks the nodes and takes ove
r outbound traffic in about two seconds.

The node table shows every node with its measured latency; click one to pin it, or
**Fastest (automa

tic)** to go back to automatic selection. **Activity log** shows what the
plugin has been doing.
### It stays off until you ask

Opening the app does **nothing**: no core process, no subscription download, no dispatcher
(~4 ms).

A previous session's "on" does not restore itself — the plugin starts closed and
waits for you to en

able it. If you would rather not think about it, the agent-memory section
below tells the agent to e
nable it when a task needs it.
### Agent memory

On install the plugin appends a short section to `$DSH_HOME/AGENTS.md` teaching the agent
that the p

roxy exists and how to turn it on. Without it the agent has no way to know, and
would keep reporting

GitHub as unreachable. It is written **once**, and only when no such
section is present — a file yo

u have since edited is never rewritten. Set
`"writeMemory": false` in `$DSH_HOME/.dsh-net-proxy/conf
ig.json` to opt out.
## Verified behaviour
Measured against a real 23-node subscription:

| Nodes ranked | 23/23 reachable, fastest ≈ 90 ms, slowest ≈ 274 ms |
| Click to live | ≈ 2 s from p

ressing *Enable* |
| Cost of app start | ≈ 4 ms, and no process started |
| Exit IP, proxy on | `5.3

4.221.111` — Tokyo, JP (Akari Networks) |
| Exit IP, proxy off | `112.50.79.219` — Guangzhou, CN (Ch

ina Mobile) |
| Failover | current node retired → walked to the next → `https://github.com` returned

200 |
| Loopback | stays direct (`127.0.0.1:19387` reached DSH itself, not the proxy) |
The core's own log is the proof that traffic went through it rather than somewhere else:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Design notes
Worth reading before changing the code — most of these were learned the hard way.

**The subscription document is never reshaped.** mihomo's YAML parser rejects duplicate
mapping keys

(stricter than the YAML spec), so prepending your own keys fails outright, and
lifting a block like

`dns:` out of the document breaks its neighbours. The plugin rewrites
only a handful of listener/co

ntroller **scalars, in place**, and leaves every block exactly
[该节后续省略]
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness desktop, Windows x64
- A Clash-format subscription link
- No admin rights, no oth

ess desktop, Windows x64
- A Clash-format subscription link
- No admin rights, no other proxy client
## Known limitations

- **Clash YAML subscriptions only.** A base64 subscription link is rejected with a clear
message; sw

itch the format in your provider's dashboard.
- **HTTP proxies only.** DSH's own proxy layer accepts

`http(s)://` URLs and the bundled core
exposes an HTTP mixed port, so this is not a practical limit

— but a SOCKS-only subscription
is not supported.
- **Model requests bypass the proxy by default**

(`proxyModelCalls: false`), so a broken node
cannot take the conversation down with it. Change it in

`config.json`.
- **The bundled core is Windows x64 only.** The plugin's own code is platform-neutra

l; `bin/` is not.
- **Geodata is not auto-updated.** It ships with the plugin; refresh it with
`tool
s/fetch-geodata.mjs` when you care.
